title: SDG 11 永續城市與社區
footer: Teacher Dom · SDG #11 Sustainable Cities and Communities 永續城市與社區

slides.eyebrow_zh: 彰化最古老的學校，遇見 SDG 11

strip.en: the year Dom's hometown became a city
strip.zh: Dom 的家鄉建市那一年

strip.en: of people will live in cities by 2050

lines.en: I come from Huntington Beach, California.
lines.zh: 我來自加州的杭廷頓海灘。

lines.en: My city became a city in 1909.
lines.zh: 我的城市在 1909 年才正式建市。

lines.en: Your school began in 1896. It is older than my whole city!
lines.zh: 你們學校 1896 年就開始了——比我整座城市還老！

slides.ask_en: Today's question: how does a city grow — and how can it grow well?
slides.ask_zh: 今天的問題：城市怎麼長大？怎樣才能長得好？

slides.q_en: How old is Chungshan Elementary this year?
slides.explain_en: 2026 − 1896 = 130. The oldest school in Changhua County!

slides.ask_en: Two cities, one ocean. Let's find out how cities grow.
slides.ask_zh: 一片海洋兩端的兩座城市。來看看城市是怎麼長大的。

stops.en: A language school opens in a temple in Lukang
stops.zh: 在鹿港地藏王廟開設語言學校

stops.en: Becomes Changhua Public School, at the Confucius Temple
stops.zh: 在彰化孔廟改制為「彰化公學校」

stops.en: Moves to its home today, at the foot of Bagua Hill
stops.zh: 遷到八卦山麓，就是今天的校地

stops.en: The North Wing becomes a historic building
stops.zh: 北棟教室登錄為歷史建築

stops.en: 130 years — and you are part of the story

slides.note_en: Your school started in Lukang and grew up in Changhua. Let's find out why that matters.
slides.note_zh: 你們學校在鹿港起步、在彰化長大。來看看這為什麼重要。

slides.head_en: You Walk Past History Every Day
slides.ask_en: The North Wing: Roman arches, over 80 years old — once the longest building in Changhua.
slides.ask_zh: 北棟教室：羅馬拱廊、超過八十歲，曾是全彰化最長的單棟建築。

slides.head_en: Once, Lukang Was Taiwan's No. 2 City
slides.head_zh: 鹿港，曾經是全台第二大城
slides.body_en: From 1784, ships sailed straight from Fujian to Lukang's harbor. It grew so big that people said: first Tainan, second Lukang, third Monga.
slides.body_zh: 1784 年起，船隻從福建直航鹿港。鹿港繁榮到大家都說：「一府、二鹿、三艋舺」。

slides.q_en: Today Lukang is a small town. Why did it stop growing?
slides.q_zh: 今天的鹿港是個小鎮。它為什麼不再長大？

options.en: Sand filled the harbor, and the railway missed it
options.zh: 港口淤積，鐵路也沒經過

options.en: A giant storm washed it away
options.zh: 一場大風暴把它沖走了

slides.explain_en: Ships could not get in, and the railway went through Changhua instead.
slides.explain_zh: 船進不來，縱貫鐵路又改走彰化。

slides.q_en: In 1734, Changhua's first city wall was made of…
slides.q_zh: 1734 年，彰化的第一道城牆是用什麼做的？
slides.explain_en: Thorny bamboo! A brick wall came in 1815 — and in 1920 it was pulled down to make way for roads.
slides.explain_zh: 莿竹！1815 年才改成磚城——1920 年又為了開路被拆掉。

slides.head_en: of all people will live in cities by 2050
slides.head_zh: 2050 年，全世界 68% 的人會住在城市
slides.body_en: Today it is 55%. Cities are growing fast — so we have to build them well.
slides.body_zh: 現在是 55%。城市長得很快——所以一定要好好地蓋。
slides.ask_en: What does a city need so that everyone can live well?
slides.ask_zh: 城市需要什麼，才能讓每個人都住得好？

slides.ask_en: Twelve writers studied here — including Lai He, the father of Taiwan's New Literature.
slides.ask_zh: 十二位文學家曾在這裡求學，包括「臺灣新文學之父」賴和。

slides.head_zh: 真的還假的？手比 ⭕ 或 ❌

items.en: Your school is older than Dom's hometown.
items.zh: 你們學校比 Dom 的家鄉還老。

items.note_en: Target 11.4: protect our cultural and natural heritage.
items.note_zh: 目標 11.4：保護我們的文化與自然遺產。

items.en: A new building is always better than an old one.
items.zh: 新建築一定比老建築好。
items.note_en: Old places hold a city's memory.
items.note_zh: 老地方保存了一座城市的記憶。

items.en: A city is just buildings and roads.
items.zh: 城市就只是建築和馬路。
items.note_en: A city is its people — like the twelve writers on your Poem Tree.
items.note_zh: 城市是人——就像你們詩文樹上的十二位文學家。

slides.ask_en: Every old place has a story: Who built it? Why here? What changed?
slides.ask_zh: 每個老地方都有故事：誰蓋的？為什麼在這裡？改變了什麼？

slides.prompt_en: If you could protect ONE old place in Changhua, which would it be?
slides.prompt_zh: 如果只能保護彰化的一個老地方，你會選哪裡？
slides.time_en: One minute each. Then I will ask two of you.
slides.time_zh: 每人一分鐘。然後我會請兩位分享。

slides.rule_en: In 30 seconds, shout out as many places in a city in English as you can. I will count!
slides.rule_zh: 30 秒內，用英文喊出越多「城市裡的地方」越好，我來數！
slides.target_zh: 要打破的班級紀錄：16 個

slides.note_en: Watch — then tell me one thing you will do for your city.
slides.note_zh: 看完之後，告訴我你願意為你的城市做的一件事。

slides.head_en: 3 Things You Can Do This Month
slides.head_zh: 這個月你可以做的 3 件事

items.en: Find one old place near your home and learn its story.
items.zh: 找一個家附近的老地方，查出它的故事。

items.en: Take a train or bus with your family instead of a car, once.
items.zh: 和家人搭一次火車或公車，代替開車。

items.en: Take care of your school — it is a historic building!
items.zh: 愛護校園——這裡是歷史建築！
老地方訴說我們的故事。

items.en: How we travel shapes our city.
items.zh: 我們怎麼移動，決定城市的樣子。

items.en: I can make my city better.
items.zh: 我可以讓我的城市變得更好。

slides.q_en: Dom's hometown, Huntington Beach, is named after a man who built…
slides.q_zh: Dom 的家鄉杭廷頓海灘，是以一位做什麼的人命名的？
slides.explain_en: Henry Huntington, a railroad businessman. Trains help cities grow — in California and in Changhua.
slides.explain_zh: 亨利・杭廷頓，一位鐵路大亨。火車讓城市長大——在加州如此，在彰化也是。

slides.body_en: Go to our School Tour page and find the Chungshan Elementary column. No sign-up, no login — tell me about an old place you love.
slides.body_zh: 到我們網站的 School Tour 頁面，找到中山國小那一欄，免註冊、免登入，告訴我一個你喜歡的老地方。
slides.sentence_en: My favorite old place is ______ because ______.
slides.sentence_zh: 我最喜歡的老地方是 ______，因為 ______。

slides.big_en:
Old places, new ideas —
a city for everyone.
slides.big_zh: 老地方，新想法——一座屬於每個人的城市。
